Le pied de page du sujet imprime le repère « GCE26/0560/2/P52 » alors que la page de garde porte « 0520 » (Commerce) et « Paper Two » : la page de garde est retenue (code_matiere 0520), l'écart du pied de page est probablement une coquille d'impression du Board.

Question 5(a)(iv) : le sujet ne dit pas si le bénéfice de 3,000,000 CFAF est avant ou après les intérêts des obligations. Lecture retenue (la plus courante dans ce programme) : les intérêts (1,000,000) et le dividende des actions de préférence (200,000) sont prélevés d'abord, et tout le reste (1,800,000) va aux actions ordinaires. Si le bénéfice était déjà net des intérêts, le dividende ordinaire serait 2,800,000 CFAF. Les autres résultats sont sans ambiguïté.

Question 5(a)(i) : « Total capital » est calculé comme la somme des trois titres, obligations comprises (68,000,000 CFAF) ; le capital-actions seul vaut 48,000,000 CFAF, et la réponse le mentionne. Les calculs ont été recalculés avec Python.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Use the information on the table below to answer the questions that follow:

| Securities | Dividend/Interest rate | Number of securities | Face value of securities (CFAF) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ordinary shares | --- | 4,000 | 10,000 |
| Preference shares | 2.5% | 8,000 | 1,000 |
| Debentures | 5% | 2,000 | 10,000 |

The company made a profit of 3,000,000 CFAF during the trading period.

Calculate;

i) Total capital of the company. (3 marks)

ii) Interest on debenture. (3 marks)

iii) Dividends on preference shares. (3 marks)

iv) Dividends to ordinary shares. (3 marks)

(12 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Working.** For each type of security, the amount of capital = number of securities $\times$ face value.

| Securities | Number | Face value (CFAF) | Capital (CFAF) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ordinary shares | 4,000 | 10,000 | 40,000,000 |
| Preference shares | 8,000 | 1,000 | 8,000,000 |
| Debentures | 2,000 | 10,000 | 20,000,000 |

**(i) Total capital of the company**

$$
\text{Total capital} = 40\,000\,000 + 8\,000\,000 + 20\,000\,000 = 68\,000\,000 \text{ CFAF}
$$

(of which share capital = 40,000,000 + 8,000,000 = 48,000,000 CFAF, and loan capital = 20,000,000 CFAF in debentures).

**(ii) Interest on debentures.** Debenture holders are lenders, so they are paid a fixed interest before any dividend:

$$
\text{Interest} = \frac{5}{100} \times 20\,000\,000 = 1\,000\,000 \text{ CFAF}
$$

**(iii) Dividends on preference shares.** Preference shareholders receive a fixed dividend before ordinary shareholders:

$$
\text{Dividend} = \frac{2.5}{100} \times 8\,000\,000 = 200\,000 \text{ CFAF}
$$

**(iv) Dividends to ordinary shares.** Ordinary shareholders take what is left of the profit after the debenture interest and the preference dividend (assuming that all the remaining profit is distributed):

$$
3\,000\,000 - 1\,000\,000 - 200\,000 = 1\,800\,000 \text{ CFAF}
$$

This is $1\,800\,000 \div 4\,000 = 450$ CFAF per ordinary share, or $\frac{1\,800\,000}{40\,000\,000} \times 100 = 4.5\%$ of the capital of the ordinary shares.

**Answers:** (i) 68,000,000 CFAF; (ii) 1,000,000 CFAF; (iii) 200,000 CFAF; (iv) 1,800,000 CFAF.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain the advantages of advertising to a manufacturer.

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Advertising is any paid message that informs and persuades people to buy a product. A manufacturer gains from it in the following ways.

1. **Increases sales and profits.** Advertising makes more people aware of the product and want it, so sales rise and so does income.
2. **Informs customers about new and improved products.** It tells the public about the existence, uses, price and place of sale of a new product, which helps to launch it successfully.
3. **Builds a brand image and customer loyalty.** A well-known brand name is trusted and customers go on buying it, even when similar goods exist.
4. **Lower cost per unit through large-scale production.** Greater demand leads to higher output; the fixed costs are spread over more units, so the cost per unit falls (economies of scale).
5. **Helps to face competition and keep or increase market share** against rival manufacturers.
6. **Persuades wholesalers and retailers to stock the goods**, because they know that customers will ask for them.
7. **Reaches a wide audience** (radio, television, posters, newspapers, social media) at a lower cost than visiting each customer.
8. **Helps to even out demand** (for example by special offers in slack seasons) and to educate customers on how to use the product.

*Any four advantages, each explained (2 marks each).*

**Conclusion.** Advertising is a cost to the manufacturer, but it normally brings in greater sales and profit than it costs.
